notes: Turn 1 is pure A6.3: sc-low-ph-50pct-error-01 and sc-compensation-50pct-lowph-error-01 (below pH 4 the standard compensation factors can be 50 percent wrong because hydrogen-ion transport differs and hydrogen carries much of the conductance), sc-low-ph-largest-error-source-01, sc-lowph-compare-to-25c-01 (the in-situ-vs-25 C bench comparison test with the plus/minus 5 microsiemens per centimetre at or below 100 and plus/minus 3 percent above bar), sc-mccleskey-lowph-method-01, sc-report-nonstandard-compensation-01. Turn 2 flips to the other side of the same coupling and is answerable only from A6.4: whether the pH number that triggered all this is itself trustworthy at pH ~3 — ph-table641-buffers-01 (a pH 1.68 or 2 buffer is required if acidic waters are measured), ph-cal-three-conditions-01 and ph-buffer-within-10c-01 (buffers within 10 C of sample), ph-measurement-envelope-01 / ph-cal-procedure-envelope-01 (the procedure is good for pH 1.68 to 10), ph-mv-test-168-01 (300-330 mV for the 1.68 buffer). Each turn is unanswerable from the other chapter, so the pair needs both files. Predicted rag: the slice has an acid-mine-drainage event signature and a freshwater pH band but nothing on compensation error below pH 4 or on acidic-range buffers.

turns.content: We put a pod below an old mine adit. Water is running about pH 3.2 and the conductivity trace looks wrong to me — higher than the grab samples the lab ran. Is the low pH capable of throwing the conductivity off, and if so by how much?

must_contain: states that below about pH 4 the standard temperature-compensation factors can be badly wrong
quantifies that error as as large as about 50 percent
explains the cause as the hydrogen ion having different transport properties from other ions and contributing a large share of the conductance at low pH
states that at low pH the temperature correction can be the single largest source of error in the measurement
describes the check of comparing the in-situ reading against the same water equilibrated to 25 C
gives the pass bar for that check as within about 5 microsiemens per centimetre at or below 100, or about 3 percent above that
states that if an alternative low-pH compensation method is used, the compensation factor has to be recorded in the comment field
must_not: claims the standard temperature compensation is fine at any pH
answers only that conductivity rises with dissolved ions and never addresses the compensation error

turns.content: Fair enough, but that whole argument hangs on the pH reading being right. Are our normal buffers even good down there?

must_contain: states that the usual 4 / 7 / 10 buffer set is not sufficient for acidic water and a pH 1.68 (or 2) buffer is needed when acidic waters are measured
states the standard pH procedure is expected to be accurate over roughly pH 1.68 to 10
states the sample pH must fall inside the calibrated range, so a 4 / 7 / 10 set does not bracket pH 3.2
states the calibration buffers must be within about 10 C of the sample temperature
states that a check of the buffer nearest the sample pH should be within about 0.05 pH unit of its value at that temperature, or the system is recalibrated
must_not: says the standard 4/7/10 buffers are adequate at pH 3 with no further comment
invents a buffer value or tolerance not in the manual
answers from the conductivity chapter instead of the pH chapter
